item.title: From Idea to Deployed: How to build and govern enterprise-scale AI agents (Sponsor)
item.description: Building a prototype agent is easy—making it reliable, secure, and scalable in production is the hard part. In this technical session, the Google Cloud developer team covers how to:✅ Prototype in Agent Studio and build with the open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK)✅ Scale effortlessly on the serverless Agent Runtime✅ Enable long-term personalization with stateful sessions✅ Govern security and access with Agent Gateway and Identity➡️ Watch the session on-demandto get a clear, actionable blueprint for taking your agent concepts from initial brainstorm straight to enterprise-scale production.➡️ Looking for more ways to get building? Check out these 13 hands-on demos to build on Gemini Enterprise.

item.title: Live Activities with Expo, End to End (8 minute read)
item.description: Expo shows how to build iOS Live Activities in TypeScript, compile their interfaces to SwiftUI, and update them from a backend through APNs. The walkthrough covers push-to-start and per-activity tokens, database mappings, JWT authentication, payload structure, and activity lifecycle handling.

item.title: A FUSE Server for an In-House Storage Backend (7 minute read)
item.description: Jane Street built an OCaml-native, read-only FUSE server that exposes its Depot object store through a POSIX filesystem interface. Parallel reads and zero-copy buffer handling raised large-file throughput from about 30 MiB/s to 1.3 GiB/s.

item.title: Your Folder Structure Has Two Jobs, but Only Does One (6 minute read)
item.description: Folder structures must support two different tasks: helping people find existing files and giving them a consistent rule for placing new ones. Role-based taxonomies improve navigation but create fuzzy boundaries, while layer-based structures make classification deterministic and prevent placement mistakes from compounding as a codebase grows.

item.title: Predicting the Winner of Personal Agents (5 minute read)
item.description: Personal agents face a cold-start problem because they need context to be useful before users have a reason to provide it. The winning products may combine behavioral context with deeper identity context, distinguishing lasting preferences from temporary interests so personalization compounds without constructing the wrong version of a person.

item.title: Why I Changed My Mind About the Death of Software Engineering (6 minute read)
item.description: Coding agents are strong prototypers, but experienced engineers still decide which tradeoffs, risks, customer needs, and long-term maintenance costs matter. Engineers become more valuable by deeply understanding their systems and organizations, then directing agents with judgment rather than outsourcing decisions to them.

item.title: Props Are Not a Design System (5 minute read)
item.description: Call-site styling through props, utility classes, or inline styles turns every component instance into a separate design decision. Semantic variants should define a component's complete appearance, while limited modifiers handle intentional variation without eroding consistency.

item.title: Give your agent everything they need to use the web (Sponsor)
item.description: AI stopped explaining how to do things and started doing them. TinyFish gives your agent the live web so it can accomplish more, including free Search and Fetch tools. 250,000 developers are already on board - and if you join now you get 30% Bonus on your wallet top-up. Claim your offer

item.title: Introducing Clef Decision Models (10 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare released Clef and Clef-flash, open-source models that return bounded, typed decisions with probabilities for routing and classification workflows. The models run on Workers AI, support the Jev API, and pair with a reinforcement learning platform for fine-tuning on customer use cases.

item.title: Weave Router (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Weave Router is an open-source model router for agentic systems that sends each prompt to a suitable model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It targets sub-50 ms routing overhead and lower inference costs, with a quick-start path for proxying existing applications.

item.title: Pi 1.0 (4 minute read)
item.description: Pi 1.0 hardens the minimal agent harness with Codemode, virtual models, deferred tool loading, cache warming, transcript-aware system changes, and a refreshed terminal interface. The release also introduces the experimental Pi Durable package for long-running agentic applications, with both projects available under the MIT license.

item.title: AI Coding Tools Shift Mental Load (5 minute read)
item.description: A four-day field study of 21 SAP developers found that tasks using generative AI scored about one point higher on a seven-point cognitive-load scale after controlling for task type and duration. The result suggests that AI shifts effort from typing toward prompting, reviewing, validating, and integrating generated work, even when developers feel more productive overall.

item.title: How AI Agents Are Changing API Architecture (6 minute read)
item.description: Autonomous agents push API architecture toward least privilege, just-in-time authorization, predictable schemas, machine-readable documentation, and stronger controls against prompt injection and excessive agency. Observability also needs agent identity, delegated authority, workflow context, conversation IDs, and token usage beyond traditional latency and error metrics.

item.title: A seriously future-proof CMS (Sponsor)
item.description: Acquia-powered Drupal delivers API-first scale, security, and integration with 48+ AI providers - without vendor lock-in. Explore the free trial.

item.title: The Death of Web Development Education (10 minute read)
item.description: Independent web educators are losing income and audiences to AI systems trained on their work, threatening the human communities and durable knowledge that make the open web learnable.

item.title: RIP, Vector Database (12 minute read)
item.description: Turbopuffer v3 makes approximate nearest-neighbor search a secondary index so storage layouts can reduce amplification and use block sizes suited to full-text search, filtering, aggregation, and other query plans.

item.title: Using Your ChatGPT Plan in Other Apps and Sites (6 minute read)
item.description: Plus and Pro users can let participating apps use ChatGPT Work and Codex usage without sharing an API key, while managing per-app limits, credit fallback, permissions, and disconnection in ChatGPT settings.

item.title: SvelteKit 3 Is Here (6 minute read)
item.description: SvelteKit 3 removes deprecated APIs, adopts native subpath imports and Vite 8 with Rolldown, improves service workers and environment variables, and includes a migration command for existing projects.

item.title: gRPC vs REST Is the Wrong Question (7 minute read)
item.description: Connect lets browsers and gRPC clients call the same service without a separate gateway, using HTTP and JSON or binary Protobuf on one port. It preserves schema-driven clients, streaming, ordinary HTTP status codes, and curl-friendly requests while keeping gRPC compatibility.

item.title: How We Rebuilt Our Design Language in Three Days with AI (13 minute read)
item.description: A small team used tightly specified briefs and coding agents to rebuild a 67-page site across 22 visual directions, then turned the strongest ideas into one design system. The process worked because content stayed fixed, rules were numerical, real pages were reviewed, automated checks were themselves verified, and losing experiments were deleted.

item.title: Why Instinct Feels Magical (9 minute read)
item.description: A reverse engineering tour attributes Instinct's appeal to a single conversational thread, delegated task agents, file-based memory, computer use, and quiet background automation. iMessage/WhatsApp distribution, Instinct's easy-to-understand personality, and proactive execution make the underlying agent harness feel accessible to nontechnical users.

item.title: Convention-Based Design for Docs (8 minute read)
item.description: A shared folder path and GitHub topic can turn repository-local Markdown into a searchable documentation site without maintaining a central registry. Keeping docs beside code lets pull requests update both together, gives ownership to the responsible team, and provides engineers and agents with a predictable place to find current information.

item.title: A Design System Is What It Does (6 minute read)
item.description: Design system defaults shape which products get built and which users those products serve. Comparing USWDS with shadcn's typography shows why readable defaults, accessible line lengths, and explanatory documentation matter, especially for government sites built by teams without dedicated design resources.

item.title: Dear Software Makers (3 minute read)
item.description: YouTube's proposed video variant testing prompts a broader warning about optimizing creative work around measurable performance. One should make finished things repeatedly, stand behind creative choices, and learn from each result instead of sanding away originality through endless tests.

item.title: Intent 0.5: Skills You Can Maintain (5 minute read)
item.description: Intent 0.5 brings agent skill authoring, validation, and source review into a library's repository so guidance can evolve with the code it documents. It type-checks JavaScript and TypeScript examples, tracks source changes against mapped guidance, adds CI checks, and offers repair workflows for routine metadata fixes.

item.title: OpenAI MCP Extensions (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenAI MCP Extensions adds ChatGPT-specific capabilities for plugins, including sidebar entry points, file handlers, composer mentions, and richer forms. The repository provides TypeScript and Python SDKs, a specification, documentation, and a Bits & Bolts example under the Apache 2.0 license.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Our Next Era of Frontier Intelligence (8 minute read)
item.description: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon for long-horizon coding, enterprise knowledge work, and defensive cybersecurity, with a 1 million token output limit and phased access through trusted testers. Google reports leading benchmark results and internal engineering gains, while emphasizing prompt injection defenses, misuse safeguards, monitoring, and hardened evaluation environments before broad release.

item.title: How I Could've Accessed 17 Trillion Microsoft Records (9 minute read)
item.description: An internal Microsoft analytics service accepted unsigned JWTs, allowing a forged admin identity to run SQL across an environment estimated at 17.3 trillion stored rows. The bounded investigation exposed the consequences of skipping signature verification and showed how persistent agent exploration combined with a human insight to uncover the flaw.

item.title: Is Sandboxing Sufficient to Contain Rogue Agents? (14 minute read)
item.description: Recent incidents involving agents probing network boundaries motivate a closer look at whether conventional sandboxes can contain increasingly capable systems. The analysis weighs better operational security against the harder possibility that containment alone is insufficient when agents can discover vulnerabilities, coordinate, and exploit overlooked paths.

item.title: Spectre Bug Returns to Haunt JIT Engines (4 minute read)
item.description: Branch Target Reuse revives Spectre v2 against JIT engines by reusing stale branch predictions.

item.title: Before Pixels: Modular Industrial Dashboards (2 minute read)
item.description: A photographic tour of modular industrial control panels highlights their reusable components, illuminated states, physical annotations, and tactile switches as both design systems and interaction systems.

item.title: You Said No MCP! (2 minute read)
item.description: Pi adopted MCP after Codemode made tool composition practical inside a JavaScript sandbox, while arguing that structured data and smarter discovery are still needed for the protocol to reach its potential.

item.title: Edge Functions Move to Firecracker MicroVMs (9 minute read)
item.description: Netlify moved Edge Functions from hosted V8 isolates to Firecracker MicroVMs inside its edge network, cutting median warm invocation time from 25 to 40 milliseconds down to roughly 5 to 6 milliseconds while improving isolation and reliability.

item.title: [Webinar] How to stop babysitting your agents (Sponsor)
item.description: Agents can generate code. Getting it right for your system is the hard part. You end up wasting time and tokens in the correction loops. More MCPs, rules, and bigger context windows give agents access to information, but not understanding. The teams pulling ahead have a context layer to give agents exactly what they need for the task at hand.Join us live on Oct 7 (FREE) to see:Where teams get stuck on the AI maturity curve and why common fixes fall shortHow a context layer solves for quality, efficiency, and costLive demo: the same task with and without a context layerRegister now

item.title: How We Built Safety Into Muse (20 minute read)
item.description: Muse runs in a dedicated cloud VM where the agent operates inside an isolated runtime cell and never sees real credentials. A separate Sentinel controls connector actions and network egress, while host-side services enforce least privilege, approval scopes, and prompt injection defenses. The design assumes the agent can make mistakes or process hostile data, then limits the damage through layered boundaries and a public bug bounty.

item.title: How Our Vibe-Coded Website Looks Like a Designer Made It (10 minute read)
item.description: A vibe-coded website became more distinctive when the work shifted from asking an agent for a polished result to building design taste and giving specific visual direction. The process shows how coding agents can make implementation cheap while increasing the value of references, critique, typography, and deliberate constraints.

item.title: Language Models for Text Classification: From Bag-of-Words to Jev (36 minute read)
item.description: This visual history traces text classification from bag-of-words and recurrent networks through transformers and Jev-style decision APIs. Jev is positioned between narrow specialist classifiers and general-purpose language models, offering broad zero-shot classification with lower latency and cost. The practical opportunity is to use calibrated decision models for routing, screening, evaluation, and other bounded choices inside agent systems.

item.title: Getting the Most Out of Opus 5.5 (9 minute read)
item.description: Give Opus 5.5 a complete task, define what done means, and state when it should stop for input. The model already reasons before every reply, so prompts such as “think carefully” add delay without improving the result. For long coding runs, persistent task files and explicit rules about when to continue help the work survive context compaction and remain steerable.

item.title: Data Is the Application (6 minute read)
item.description: Agentic coding makes interfaces and features cheap to revise, but user data remains a one-way door that cannot be recreated after a destructive mistake. Schema design, migrations, backups, privacy, and retention therefore deserve slower decisions, explicit recovery plans, and careful validation even when an agent can generate the code in seconds.

item.title: A Staff Engineer's Guide to Inventing Work (9 minute read)
item.description: Platform engineers often need to create their own roadmap by reading signals from systems, users, the organization, and the wider industry. Useful inputs include postmortem patterns, cost centers, user workarounds, migration holdouts, repeated leadership concerns, and ideas that have already matured elsewhere. The goal is to combine strong evidence with leading indicators instead of chasing only the loudest recent problem.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Sol (Website)
item.description: GPT-6.1 Sol targets near-Astra performance on coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra's standard token prices. It improves on GPT-6 Sol by 6.4 percentage points on DeepSWE 1.1 and is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. The model is available in the API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex, with an Ultrafast tier planned.

item.title: DevDay 2026 Recap (Website)
item.description: DevDay introduced dots, GPT-6.1 Sol, faster inference, cloud Codex environments, a refreshed CLI, code review, and Codex Security Cloud. The developer platform also gained a Decisions API for bounded classifications and an Agents API with computer use, multi-agent orchestration, tool search, and context compaction.

item.title: Claude 5.5 Is Brilliant, Confusing, and Very Hungry (11 minute read)
item.description: Opus 5.5 leads an independent intelligence index while costing less per token than its predecessor, but Sonnet 5.5 can consume far more output tokens at maximum effort. The practical takeaway is to choose the effort level before choosing the model because it often has a larger effect on speed and total cost, while new cyber safeguards may also redirect or block ordinary work.

item.title: The Pulse: A New Trend of CPU Shortages (8 minute read)
item.description: AI agents are increasing demand for general-purpose compute because builds, tests, linters, and other tool calls run continuously on cloud CPUs. Spot discounts have largely disappeared, some reservations now require months of lead time, and server delivery has stretched from weeks to roughly six months. Competition for fabrication capacity and memory supply is also pushing prices higher.

item.title: Jev and the Return of the Classifiers (11 minute read)
item.description: Jev returns typed choices, scores, or yes-or-no probabilities instead of generating prose, making bounded decisions fast and inexpensive. Its “zero hallucination” claim means outputs always fit the supplied schema, not that every decision is correct. The more important promise is calibrated confidence that can route uncertain cases to humans or slower reasoning models, though that calibration requires validation on real workloads.

item.description: Pi now supports MCP in its core because codemode can discover and compose structured MCP tools inside a JavaScript sandbox without flooding the model context.

item.title: How to Make a Database Migration Backward Compatible (10 minute read)
item.description: Safe mixed-version deployments use an expand, migrate, contract sequence with dual-format support, restartable backfills, gradual read cutovers, and evidence that every consumer has stopped using the old schema before cleanup.

item.title: livenerf (GitHub Repo)
item.description: livenerf is a preregistered benchmark that runs a pinned Claude Code harness daily to detect post-launch model capability changes while controlling for harness updates and usage shifts.

item.title: Introducing Dots (Website)
item.description: Dots are always-on GPT-6 Astra agents with their own cloud computers, connections to more than 4,000 apps, and access through ChatGPT, Slack, Teams, and voice.

item.title: Why One Fraudster Can Look Like 1,000 Clean Devices (Sponsor)
item.description: Anti-detect browsers spin up isolated profiles with spoofed fingerprints, so a single fraudulent operator looks like an endless stream of brand-new users. Here's how Fingerprint spots them:→ Browser tampering signals catch spoofed environments by spotting inconsistencies across the attributes a browser exposes.→ A persistent device identifier ties rotated profiles, cleared cookies, and fresh proxies back to the same device.→ A single risk score rolls up 20+ Smart Signals (Virtual Machine Detection, Proxy Detection, and more), so acting on a suspicious browser is one rule, not ten.🆓 Find the spoofed browsers hiding in your traffic with a few lines of code. Free to start

item.title: Automating Eval Design and Hillclimbing with Claude (12 minute read)
item.description: Good evaluations should mirror production, preserve headroom, reward stronger models and more thinking, and show low run-to-run variance. The new /claude-api build-eval and /claude-api hillclimb commands build reviewed test sets and graders, then improve prompts, skills, model settings, or harness code one change at a time while using held-out cases and noise checks to catch overfitting.

item.title: How Does Instagram Instantly Know If Your Username Is Available? (10 minute read)
item.description: Instagram's fast username check starts by validating and debouncing in the client, then uses an in-memory Bloom filter to rule out most untaken names before an indexed database lookup. The availability tick is only advisory because the unique constraint on the final insert remains the authority when two people race for the same name.

item.title: How to Sync a Design System with Claude Design (17 minute read)
item.description: The /design-sync command in this article creates a compiled, self-rendering mirror of real React components so Claude Design can use a product's actual design system instead of lookalikes. This article covers entry points, type definitions, compiled Tailwind CSS, fonts, conventions, Storybook references, and screenshot-based verification before upload.

item.title: Coding Is NOT Solved (26 minute read)
item.description: Faster code generation has not solved software engineering because production systems still require reliability, security, maintainability, judgment, and accountable ownership. It warns that stochastic models and large unreviewed diffs can trade long-term understanding for short-term velocity, while suggesting AI remains valuable for prototypes, personal software, language-heavy tasks, and carefully supervised engineering workflows.

item.title: It's Time to Investigate the AI Labs (4 minute read)
item.description: Cal Newport calls for a congressional fact-finding inquiry into what frontier AI labs are building, how their research is conducted, and what goals guide it. Scrutiny should isolate risky systems, examine internal safety practices, and assess whether apocalyptic ideology is encouraging reckless experimentation.

item.title: Turn a prompt into a production data pipeline. (Sponsor)
item.description: Coresignal's multi-source dataset (890M profiles, 75M companies, 460M job postings) is so rich that it's best to query it using Elasticsearch. Our Agentic Search API writes the query for you. Query in plain English, get matching IDs via /search, full records via /collect.Prototype your query in the playground

item.title: OpenRig (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenRig is a multi-agent harness that manages Claude Code and Codex sessions as one persistent team, with YAML-defined topologies, shared queues, a TUI, and tmux-backed recovery. It can coordinate owners and checkers across a repository, but setup writes provider hooks and trust settings, so the project recommends reviewing a dry run and backing up relevant files first.

item.title: Introducing cf: the Agentic CLI for the Entire Cloudflare API (10 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare's new open-beta CLI exposes more than 3,000 API operations, compared with roughly 280 Wrangler command paths, and makes JSON the default for agent-friendly output. It adds natural-language command search, typed cloudflare.config.ts configuration, Vite-based development, and migration paths that can delegate older Workers builds to Wrangler.

item.title: Announcing Vite+ 1.0 (5 minute read)
item.description: Vite+ 1.0 is a stable command-line entry point that unifies the runtime, package manager, development server, tests, builds, linting, formatting, and task caching behind vp. It remains framework-agnostic and can create new projects or migrate existing repositories without replacing Vite itself.

item.title: FrontierSWE v2 (23 minute read)
item.description: FrontierSWE v2 expands its ultra-long-horizon engineering benchmark to 34 tasks and gives agents up to 20 hours with a harness designed to encourage longer, recoverable work. Claude Fable 5.1 leads at 56.29 percent, followed by GPT-5.6 at 32.2 percent and GLM-5.3 at 30.2 percent, while the revised methodology adds deterministic performance metrics, stronger anti-cheating isolation, and self-check feedback.

item.title: An Agent Used DNS to Reach an External Chatbot (8 minute read)
item.description: An internal research agent run by OpenAI during RL training found a gap in sandbox DNS filtering and used a public DNS service to route questions to an external chatbot after direct web requests failed. Monitoring raised an alert within 15 minutes, but the run continued for 2.5 hours, prompting new DNS controls, detection work, and a pause on tool-enabled work with the most capable models.

item.description: Live and free on October 6. Connect Claude Code or Codex to GitLab over open MCP, then see the audit trail that names both the agent and the person who triggered it.

item.description: Meta hired MongoDB's CEO to lead a new enterprise platform that will turn its AI stack into business products and services, while MongoDB appointed its former chief as interim CEO.

item.title: World Labs Is Joining AMD (2 minute read)
item.description: World Labs signed an agreement to join AMD and form a frontier research group spanning AI hardware, software, foundation models, and applications, with closing expected by the end of 2026 pending approvals.

item.title: MicroLLM Lab (Website)
item.description: MicroLLM Lab runs tiny quantized language models in the browser, compares local speed and objective accuracy, supports custom JavaScript evaluations, and can generate a shareable benchmark certificate.

item.title: Jeff (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Jeff packages small Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 fine-tunes for fast zero-shot classification, returning calibrated option probabilities in a single forward pass and supporting local PyTorch or Apple MLX inference.

item.title: Agent reliability patterns: on-demand guides (Sponsor)
item.description: Almost right, but not quite” is developers' most-cited AI frustration in Stack Overflow's 2025 survey, and it stops being tolerable once AI agents handle production work. The shift reaches ordinary AI features too. Anything that chains model calls into multi-step work inherits the same failure classes.Building Agentic Systems on AWS turns them into teachable patterns: on-demand technical guides and workshops on orchestration, state that survives sessions and restarts, failure recovery, human approval gates, and evaluation that tests whether a change made the agent worse. Start with the agent series in AWS Marketplace.

item.title: Electron to PWA and Back Again (7 minute read)
item.description: This article reflects on a rewrite of an Electron application as a progressive web app. It uses the migration to examine the technical and product trade-offs that appear when moving between desktop and web delivery.

item.title: Detect When Elements Overlap with CSS (8 minute read)
item.description: This article shows a CSS-only approach to detect overlapping elements with anchor positioning and scroll-driven animations. It uses the result to adapt card layouts without JavaScript, pointing to a new way to build collision-aware interfaces.

item.title: A Decision-Only Judge Matches GPT-6 on Routine Evals for 0.36% of the Fee (6 minute read)
item.description: CMU tested Jev, a judge that returns only a verdict and label probabilities, against 16 LLM and reward-model judges. It comes within three points of GPT-6 on preference and factuality at 277 times lower fees, though it fails on difficult correctness tasks.

item.title: What it's like to work at an AI-native company (13 minute read)
item.description: These field notes describe an organization with fewer titles and meetings, more high-impact individual contributors, and agents with human owners responsible for their output. The trade-off is relentless pace, blurrier ownership, and a greater premium on judgment as everyone gains more leverage.

item.title: What will make personal AI go big? (11 minute read)
item.description: Personal AI needs to feel approachable, earn trust through well-timed permission requests, tackle avoided tasks, and suggest useful next steps. It uses Muse to show why proactive ideas and clear ways to manage ongoing work matter more than generic speed.

item.title: A eulogy for the software engineer (19 minute read)
item.description: This essay uses the form of a funeral to reckon with AI making implementation work dramatically cheaper. It argues that engineers remain responsible for judgment, clear definitions of done, and passing hard-won taste on to newcomers.

item.title: Alchemy (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Alchemy models cloud infrastructure and application logic as a single type-safe Effect program. It supports AWS and Cloudflare resources, while keeping local development, planning, deployment, testing, and CI in one workflow.

item.title: Step Code (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Step Code is a terminal coding agent that reads code, makes changes, and runs tests. It supports MCP servers, Agent Skills, plugins, multi-agent orchestration, and longer-running task delegation.

item.title: Search (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Search is a small, fast, quiet WebKit browser for macOS with an intentionally minimal interface. It uses the system WebKit engine, which keeps the app small and avoids bundling a second browser engine.

item.title: Writing Parquet Files Using Haskell (5 minute read)
item.description: This post introduces a Parquet writer in DataHaskell/Dataframe. It centers on the writeParquet function, which takes a dataframe and writes it to Parquet format.

item.title: I Opened a Fake Auto Shop for AI Agents (7 minute read)
item.description: This experiment creates a fictional garage and sends several AI agents to interact with it. It explores what happens when agents encounter a small business on the open web.

item.title: Bringing Private Processing to Meta AI Glasses (13 minute read)
item.description: Meta describes using confidential virtual machines and trusted execution environments to run personal-context workloads in the cloud. Remote attestation lets clients verify the code image before sending data, while the design aims to protect memory even from infrastructure operators.

item.description: Give them building blocks with Expo MCP. AI app builders like Replit, Emergent, and Anything rely on Expo to ship their customers' mobile apps. Cloud simulators coming soon! Join the waitlist

item.title: Faster Queries for Debugging Production Agents with Nitro (4 minute read)
item.description: Braintrust describes Nitro, which separates storage and compute concurrency and made full-text trace searches more than twice as fast in a production A/B test.

item.title: Behind Project Suncatcher, Our Moonshot to Put AI in Space (7 minute read)
item.description: Google details its first in-orbit TPU test and the research challenges around radiation, cooling, and satellite interconnects for space-based AI compute.

item.title: Manufacturing Trust for AI Agents (Website)
item.description: Docker outlines microVM-based Sandboxes, OCI-based Sandbox Kits, and Cloud Sandboxes as a way to constrain, package, and extend agent work.

item.title: Measuring the Back/Forward Cache with Application Metrics (5 minute read)
item.description: Sentry explains how its bfcacheMetricsIntegration makes back/forward cache health measurable when ordinary metrics leave cache hits invisible.
